title: The structure-morphism mate with the identity factor
statement:
Use the Poincare duality data [def-pod-conventions] at any of the four coefficient stages. Let $a:X\to s=\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the exceptionally admissible structure morphism, let $a_s=\operatorname{id}_s$, and use the ordinary and exceptional adjunctions [fix-prop-adjunctions]. Put $w=Ra_s^!\Lambda_s$ and $\omega=Ra^!\Lambda_s$. Let $u:w\xrightarrow{\sim}\Lambda_s$ be the identity-adjunction counit isomorphism of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex]. Form the canonical mate
$$m:Ra^!Ra_s^!\Lambda_s\xrightarrow{\sim}R(a_s\circ a)^!\Lambda_s=\omega$$
of the compact-support composition comparison [thm-sf-comp-composition], with the pasted exceptional units and counits of [fix-prop-adjunctions](3). Under the identity normalization of $Ra_{s!}$ and its right adjoint, this specified mate satisfies $m=Ra^!u$. This assertion uses completed adjunctions integrally, their scalar localization at $E$, and their common finite-stage forms at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$.

source.place: Step 1, the composite-adjunction mate at a_Y = id_s, with its identity normalization

proof.text: Work in the full bounded constructible finite-Tor categories of [def-pod-conventions]. Write $F=Ra_!$, $G=Ra^!$, $I=Ra_{s!}$ and $J=Ra_s^!$. The hypotheses on $a$ give $F\dashv G$ with unit $\nu$ and counit $\mu$ by [fix-prop-adjunctions](2). For the point identity, [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients] supplies the constructible adjunction $I\dashv J$ directly. Let $v:I\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{id}$ be [lem-pod-identity-compact-support-normalization]. After replacing $I$ by the identity through this specified $v$, its adjunction counit is the natural isomorphism $u_L:J L\to L$ of [lem-pod-point-dualizing-complex]; in unnormalized notation this is $\mu_{s,L}\circ v_{J L}^{-1}$. In particular $u_{\Lambda_s}$ is exactly the $u$ in the statement. Retain $J$ and this counit in the calculation, rather than replace $J$ by an unspecified isomorphic functor.

source.place: Step 1, specialized to the identity structure morphism of the point

proof.text: At finite coefficients [thm-sf-comp-composition] gives the actual composition map $\alpha_{a_s,a}:IF\to F$ and says that it is the identity under the canonical identity identifications. Thus $\alpha_{a_s,a}=vF$. This applies to the bounded constructible inputs here: they have etale-origin witnesses by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii), and boundedness implies bounded below. The composite is again $a$, so the exceptional hypothesis for the composite is the one already assumed for $a$.

source.place: Step 1, specialized to the identity structure morphism of the point

proof.text: The same left-functor identity holds for completed integral composition, as an equality of actual maps. In the simultaneous semilinear-system construction of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization], take the identity compactification $(\operatorname{id}_s,\operatorname{id}_s)$ for the second morphism and any compactification for $a$. The proper/open square then has identity horizontal arrows. By [lem-sf-ambient-proper-open-pasting] its interchange is the identity comparison, and its proper and open compositors are unital. Hence the resulting system composition map is the identity unitor. The realization isomorphisms $c_V$ of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization] intertwine these composition maps, units, counits and their whiskerings, including nested compact supports. Consequently the realized compositor $IF\to F$ is $vF$, where integrally $v$ is the inverse of the reduction/total-limit unit as specified in [lem-pod-identity-compact-support-normalization]. All intermediate inputs here are the normalized systems of bounded constructible finite-Tor objects: preservation by $F,G$ is [lem-sf-constructible-exceptional-adjunction-coefficients], and $I$ is the identity after normalization. At $E$ apply raw scalar localization to this equality, and at $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ use its common finite coefficient-field representative. These are precisely the scalar and common-stage normalizations of the cited identity lemma; they give the same identity unitor at those stages. No assertion that finite evaluation detects equality of derived morphisms is used.

source.place: Step 1, specialized to the identity structure morphism of the point

proof.text:
Fix any of the four stages and use the normalization $I=\operatorname{id}$ just verified. The pasted adjunction for $IF\dashv GJ$ has counit $u_L\circ\mu_{J L}:FGJ L\to L$, by [fix-prop-adjunctions](3), equivalently [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. The comparison $m_L:GJ L\to G L$ in the question is the inverse of the conjugate of $\alpha_{a_s,a}$. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] this inverse is the conjugate of $\alpha_{a_s,a}^{-1}$. The latter left-adjoint map is now the identity of $F$. Substitution into the displayed component formula for the conjugate in that definition gives
$$m_L=G(u_L\circ\mu_{J L})\circ\nu_{GJ L}.$$
This uses the composite counit as source and the adjunction $F\dashv G$ as target, so the direction is $GJ\to G$, as required.

Functoriality and the right triangle identity for $F\dashv G$ in [fix-prop-adjunctions](2) now give, for every $L$ in the point category,
$$m_L=G(u_L)\circ G(\mu_{J L})\circ\nu_{GJ L}=G(u_L)\circ\operatorname{id}_{GJ L}=G(u_L).$$
Evaluate at $L=\Lambda_s$. Since $J\Lambda_s=w$, $G\Lambda_s=\omega$ and $u_{\Lambda_s}=u$, this is $m=Ra^!u$. The calculation took place in the chosen adjunctions at each stage, including the completed integral adjunction and the localized/common-stage ones; it therefore proves the equality with exactly the coefficient conventions of the statement.
